source_en: Home to the harbor flats after a night of cards at the Metropol.
Resident, harbor flats. Cards ran until dawn, going home to sleep.
Meeting a friend to settle a sports debt.
Back from the basement game by the tram depot. Going home.
Checking on the security of my hidden "nest egg."
The Metropol is shut. Going home to count what I have left.
Folded early at the cellar game. Back to my bunk for lockdown.
Going home to fold my hand. Harbor block, lockdown bunk.
Mandatory resident check-in. The odds say I should show up.
Teller at the State Savings Bank. Day shift, home by six.
Visiting the city for the week. My home address is in Batumi.
Handing in my pension papers at the district office.
Going to the Metropol card room. Open every night now.
Off duty from the militia post. Back on the beat tomorrow.
Moving in with an uncle. First time living in the city.
Novice at the monastery. Returning to my cell for prayers.
Retired at sixty-five. Collecting my veteran's ration card.
Arriving from Poti to register as a new city resident.
Heads or tails, officer? Just kidding. Here are my documents.
I’m betting on a quick recovery for the city. The spread looks good.
You have a "poker face" that would bankrupt me in ten minutes.
I put everything on the "red sky" theory. Looks like I’m cleaning up.
Here’s the form. I like my chances today; I found a four-leaf clover in the ash.
The house always wins, doesn't it? And right now, the house is falling down.
One last spin of the wheel. Let's see if my ID still carries any value.
I’m going home to fold my hand. There’s no out-bluffing the end of the world.
Luck is a lady, but she’s left town on the last bus.
My lucky streak continues! See you at the next turn.
Thanks. I’ll give you 5-to-1 odds that you’re still here tomorrow.
The stakes are too high for me now. Take care of yourself.
Put me in the corner pocket? Fine, as long as I can keep my cards.
I’ve spent time in worse rooms than this. Is there a light?
A dead end. I should have seen that coming. The math doesn't lie.
I guess... my luck... finally... ran out...
That’s... a hell... of a... bad beat...
Busted... out of... the game... at last.
All right, all right. Corner pocket. I’ve bluffed my way out of worse hands.
Two-to-one I’m out of here by morning. I like those odds.
One bad hand. That's all this is. Every player has bad hands.
Funny… I had three aces… and it still wasn’t enough…
I miscalculated somewhere… the math… the math was wrong…
House always wins in the end… I should have… bet on that…
Where are you coming from?
The back room of the Metropol. Cards until dawn. Now home to the harbor flats to sleep it off.
The Metropol shut when the curfew started. There is a basement game near the tram depot. Low stakes, bad light.
A cellar across the river. Last game in town, three players and one candle. I folded early. Back to my bunk now.
Off the evening train from Kutaisi. First time in your town, officer. They tell me the Metropol runs a good game.
My shift at the port, loading freighters. Honest work now, officer. I gave up the cards years ago.
The Metropol. They opened the card room again, full tables all night. Best game I have seen in months.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Sweaty palms, same as always. Bad for holding cards, good for bluffing. Otherwise nothing.
I sleep all afternoon and still wake up tired. Headaches when the numbers will not sit still. Nothing the polyclinic can fix.
I forget hands now. Whole hands. Twenty years I never forgot a card. Write that down however you like.
Nothing. Dry hands, steady as a surgeon. Always been that way, even at the table.
Never better. No late nights since I quit the cards, so no headaches either. I sleep like a Party official.
Nothing. At forty-five a man learns to pace himself, officer. I rest, I eat, I stay out of trouble.
Heads or tails, officer? Just kidding. I know when the odds are against me.
You have a poker face that would bankrupt me in ten minutes. I mean that as a compliment.
I put everything on a quick recovery for the city. The spread looked good at the time.
The house always wins, does it not? And right now the house is on fire.
I found a four-leaf clover in the ash this morning. Taking that as a sign.
The odds keep shifting. I keep adjusting. That is all you can do.
I am going home to fold my hand. There is no out-bluffing the end of the world.
Luck is a lady but she left on the last bus out.
Every player knows when to walk away from the table. I am almost there.
